# swo_circleci_integration (Resource)

A Terraform resource for managing CircleCI integrations with SWO for webhook-based CI/CD pipeline monitoring and log aggregation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# 1. Create the SWO CircleCI integration
resource "swo_circleci_integration" "main" {
  name      = "My Organization"
  api_token = "CIRCLECI_API_TOKEN_VALUE" # Optional: CircleCI API token for log aggregation
  receiver_base = "https://webhook.swo.XX.solarwinds.com/webhook" # Optional: Prefix for receiver_url. SWO endpoint where your organization is monitored.
}

# 2. For each CircleCI project, add or remove webhook blocks as needed
resource "circleci_webhook" "service_a" {
  name           = "SolarWinds Observability"
  url            = swo_circleci_integration.main.receiver_url
  signing_secret = swo_circleci_integration.main.secret_token
  scope_id       = "PROJECT_ID"  # Replace with actual CircleCI project ID
  scope_type     = "project"
  events         = ["workflow-completed", "job-completed"] # SWO requires both workflow-completed and job-completed events
  verify_tls     = true # SWO requires TLS certificate verification
  is_active      = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The user-provided name of the CircleCI integration. Used to identify the integration in SWO.

### Optional

- `api_token` (String, Sensitive) The CircleCI API token for enhanced log aggregation. If not provided, webhook reception still works but log fetching will be unavailable.
- `receiver_base` (String) Prefix used to construct `receiver_url`. Set this to the SWO webhook endpoint where your organization is monitored.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the CircleCI integration.
- `receiver_url` (String) The receiver URL to configure in CircleCI project webhook settings.
- `secret_token` (String, Sensitive) The secret token to configure in CircleCI project webhook settings.

## Webhook Configuration

After creating the integration, configure webhooks in your CircleCI projects using the [CircleCI Terraform provider's `circleci_webhook` resource](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/CircleCI-Public/circleci/latest/docs/resources/webhook):

```terraform
resource "circleci_webhook" "my_webhook" {
  name           = "SolarWinds Observability"
  url            = swo_circleci_integration.main.receiver_url
  signing_secret = swo_circleci_integration.main.secret_token
  scope_id       = "PROJECT_ID"  # Replace with your CircleCI project UUID
  scope_type     = "project"
  events         = ["workflow-completed", "job-completed"] # SWO requires both
  verify_tls     = true # SWO requires TLS certificate verification
  is_active      = true
}
```

For multiple projects, use `for_each`:

```terraform
resource "circleci_webhook" "projects" {
  for_each = toset(var.circleci_project_ids)

  name           = "SolarWinds Observability"
  url            = swo_circleci_integration.main.receiver_url
  signing_secret = swo_circleci_integration.main.secret_token
  scope_id       = each.value
  scope_type     = "project"
  events         = ["workflow-completed", "job-completed"]
  verify_tls     = true
  is_active      = true
}
```

## Notes

- The `api_token` is stored securely in the backend and not returned in subsequent reads; Terraform will only track if it was explicitly set.
- Updating `name` or `api_token` does not regenerate the `receiver_url` or `secret_token`.
- Deleting the resource in Terraform removes the integration from SWO.
